observations: Two retail boxes for EDON LV-400 welding machines are shown stacked.
The boxes are labeled 'DC INVERTER MMA WELDER'.
The model 'LV-400' is printed prominently on the boxes in photo 0.
The packaging claims the device is 'AVAILABLE AT LOW VOLTAGE (LOW VOLTAGE FROM 160V-265V)'.
Icons on the box indicate cable lengths of 2M, 1.8M, and 1.2M.
The actual welding machine is not visible; only the cardboard packaging is shown.

claims.evidence: The model name LV-400 on the box in photo 0 suggests 400 amps, but the actual output rating on the machine's technical plate is not visible.
The voltage range 160V-265V shown on the box in photo 0 is consistent with single-phase power, but it is not explicitly stated.

risks.risk: The box may be empty or contain a different, lower-value item.
risks.proof: Photo of the actual welding machine outside of its packaging.

risks.risk: The machine may be used or have physical damage hidden by the box.
risks.proof: Clear photos of the machine's casing, terminals, and cooling vents.

risks.risk: The internal inverter components may be faulty or non-functional.
risks.proof: Video of the machine powered on and striking an arc.

proof_requests: Photo of the actual welding machine outside the box.
Photo of the technical specification plate located on the machine.
Photo of all included accessories such as the electrode holder and earth clamp.
Video of the machine powered on and welding.
response.reason: Only the retail packaging is visible in the photo. It is impossible to verify the presence, condition, or authenticity of the machine without seeing the unit itself.
